outputs.summary: Acceptance is now terminal on every import path. The rule lives in the importer, so the reconcile, run Keep tracked (its reconcile) and epic Keep tracked (its reconcile) all go through it, with no per-caller copy. (1) upsertAttempt's ON CONFLICT update has a WHERE clause: it never overwrites an attempt that is accepted here and not superseded with a tracked copy that is not 'accepted'. A tracked copy that is accepted (superseded by revision adoption or not) is still written, and so is any copy of an attempt not accepted here or superseded here. (2) After a run is applied, applyRun finds the acceptances the tracked record does not hold as accepted and not superseded, using DM-388's acceptanceTrackedLacks: the ones it kept, plus any the record lacks entirely. If there are any, it queues the run's run_history export and leaves those attempts' search entries alone. (3) upsertTicketStatuses no longer writes a tracked status that would move a ticket completed here back. Such tickets are held. Once every run of the reconcile has been applied, settleCompletedTickets keeps a held ticket completed, and queues the epic_state export, only while the ticket's newest acceptance among the epic's runs (latest run, then latest attempt) is not superseded. Otherwise the ticket takes its tracked status. (4) If a later reconcile's run import supersedes an acceptance that was standing here, and the run's revision still plans that ticket, a ticket still completed with no standing acceptance moves to in_progress (as the other machine's adoption left it) and the epic export is queued. enqueueOutbox now takes Pick<Ctx,'db'|'clock'> so the importer can queue exports. docs/architecture.md gains one sub-bullet under the epic bullet and one under the run bullet.

A 'keep' is re-decided each time, from the scan's own read of unchanged epics. Nothing is persisted, and no file is read outside the scan except the backing run's run.json, behind a catch-all that maps to 'keep'. Where R1-R3 could disagree, and what was checked. The run export from applyRun lands on the file just imported (markSynced first), so unimportedRunHistory passes. No export is queued over another machine's unimported file (s1). Kept/deferred states record no conflict, and storeConflicts is untouched (no s3). 'Own export' is exported_hash = hash AND imported_hash IS NULL. (3) hasAcceptedAttempt (any standing acceptance, by hand) vs NEWEST_ACCEPTANCE (automatic). The automatic rule never reverses a tracked completion, so a person's hand completion on an older acceptance survives (E4 x2 and the re-exported-hand-completion test). After B's Write local, A's reconcile keeps attempt a accepted with A's notes and keeps ticket 1 completed, with no conflict. It queues run_history and epic_state, and the next reconcile has no conflict. A flushes 2 entries holding a and b accepted and both tickets completed. B's submit succeeds, auto_continue and orchestrator_session_id are kept, and B's next export imports on A with no conflict. Fails on 8483b39 and 15452fe. Still passing at 2a13258; failed on 8483b39.

Guards: same-reconcile adoption; earlier-run acceptance; the plan-changed test, where the later run supersedes and the ticket takes in_progress; E6, where a tracked superseded copy takes the tracked status; the unreadable-run and partial-pull tests, which take the other machine's status once its run supersedes. T2: 'epic Keep tracked keeps B's completed ticket that its accepted attempt backs, and exports it' (both variants). E6: a ticket whose acceptance the other machine's history holds superseded takes its status, and the not-accepted one is kept and exported. The ticket completed by an unexported local run is kept and exported. The newer-history describe keeps without export, then exports after the run is settled by either choice. evidence.notes:
Masked builders and callers of epic ticket status: buildEpicStateRecord, which finalizer exportEpic reaches for every epic_state flush (person edits, Write local's own flush, settlement exports, Keep-tracked follow-ups); and transfers buildCurrentPacket, which queueTransfer reaches. Red-team 3 confirmed the finalizer is the only state.json writer. Comment and run-history files carry no ticket status. Attacked:
- Fixed, with tests: an epic deleted by the other machine; a branch round trip; a branch-change reconcile importing the settling run (rt4 Q2).
- Holds that wait: epics that are missing, rejected, transfer-held, in conflict or failed to apply; and an unreadable epics/, where nothing settles (rt3 P7).
- Masked: leaks within the same reconcile and in later exports (leak probes x2); Write local (test); the Linear packet (test).
- Hand completion while held releases the hold and exports completed. Hand move back is still refused. Adoption here clears the hold via the trigger.
- An unreadable run or unparsable plan gives keep and never throws.
- A ticket deleted from the plan keeps its row and hold until settled; the docs now say so.
- Idle cost: an indexed held query, with no re-parse.
Every new branch is test-covered and mutation-checked. Branch decision: a branch-change reconcile settles holds of unchanged epics by the same rules as the next same-branch reconcile would (red-team round 4 showed that skipping only lost the imported run's evidence). So a held completion can go out into a branch whose run.json lacks its acceptance. That is the existing lingering-rows limitation, documented in the run rule and listed in discoveries.

outputs.summary: Attempt 3. The rule lives in one place, importer.ts. An import never moves an attempt this machine accepted, and has not superseded, back, and never moves back a ticket that such an acceptance completed. Attempt 2 was rejected for two reasons. A completion kept without export leaked out with any unrelated epic_state export. And the settlement re-parsed every unchanged epic on every reconcile. Attempt 3 adds a held marker, ticket_status.held_status (schema v12): a nullable column with a CHECK, a partial index, and a trigger that clears it whenever the ticket moves off completed. A held ticket stays completed locally, but every export of the epic writes the held status instead, through exportedTicketStatuses. That covers the finalizer's state.json for any flush (Write local and the settlement's own exports included) and the Linear transfer packet. Settlement is an indexed query over held rows plus this reconcile's held statuses, judged by verdictOf (take / keep / export). Read and parse failures map to keep, so the settlement never throws. Completing a held ticket by hand releases the hold and exports completed. Red-team 3 found that holds of an epic missing from the checkout (deleted by the other machine) were settled and wrote the epic back. It also found that a branch change reverted holds, losing completions on a round trip, and that a docs sentence was wrong. Fixed in 30a2f24 and 2a13258: earlier holds settle only for epics the reconcile found unchanged and does not skip (an imported epic's tickets arrive through upsertTicketStatuses). All other holds wait. A branch-change reconcile settles by the same rules, instead of reverting or skipping, so a run imported then is not lost to the settlement. The docs are corrected.

discoveries.body: EpicSecurityReview F1 (medium): unimportedRunHistory/unimportedProfile and their callers (finalizer, importer planRejectedRuns, profileImport, storage, runConflict, profileConflict) read and hash the whole tracked file on every flush, reconcile and heartbeat while an export waits, under BEGIN IMMEDIATE (64 MiB: ~2 s per heartbeat); ~86 MB of control bytes makes the hash throw RangeError, so no conflict is shown and both choices throw.
